title: Transboundary Haze Enforcement and Corporate Accountability
topic_prompt: Following the severe 2026 transboundary haze crisis that drove air quality across Singapore into the Very Unhealthy range (PSI > 200) and prompted NEA to issue Section 10 notices under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA), intense debate has erupted over the government's response. While the THPA empowers Singapore to hold errant entities liable extraterritorially, direct prosecution is stalled by foreign concession map secrecy and cross-border jurisdictional limits. One participant demands aggressive unilateral legal prosecution and punitive financial retaliation against regional plantation conglomerates, while the other emphasizes diplomatic caution, sovereign non-interference, and cooperative firefighting assistance. Deliberate to find common ground.

ballot.prompt: Based on your deliberation, select the single policy resolution that best represents your preferred path forward:

options.A: Combine bilateral firefighting assistance and ASEAN satellite data-sharing with domestic regulatory leverage: enforce strict MAS/SGX sustainable finance taxonomies and mandatory supply-chain traceability that cut off Singapore-based bank lending, capital market access, and public procurement for agribusinesses linked to burning. (Key - Integrative Compromise)
options.B: Rely exclusively on diplomatic appeals and routine offers of regional firefighting assistance through ASEAN channels, accepting periodic transboundary haze as an unavoidable meteorological condition without pursuing corporate accountability. (Distractor 1 - Status Quo Inertia)
options.C: Unilaterally issue extraterritorial arrest warrants and freeze Singapore-based bank accounts of regional plantation executives regardless of diplomatic fallout, prioritizing punitive optics over bilateral environmental cooperation. (Distractor 2 - Technocratic Zero-Sum)
options.D: Impose blanket retaliatory tariffs on all agricultural imports from neighboring countries and deflect domestic public health obligations by blaming external governments entirely. (Distractor 3 - External Scapegoating/Deflection)
